Last Trump
last trump
noun phrase (1 Corinthians 15:52)
From “trump” (a trumpet), through Old French trompe; the final trumpet-blast of God at the resurrection and return of Christ.

📖 Biblical Definition

The last trump is the final trumpet-blast that shall sound at the coming of Christ, summoning the dead to rise and the living to be changed. The apostle reveals the mystery: “We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.” Paul tells the Thessalonians that the Lord Himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God, and the dead in Christ shall rise first. Our Lord foretold that He shall send His angels with a great sound of a trumpet to gather His elect from the four winds. The trumpet runs back through Scripture as the signal of God's presence and summons—at Sinai, in the jubilee, in the assembling of Israel—and here it is the signal of the consummation. The dictionary holds the last trump to teach the bodily resurrection and the instantaneous transformation of the living saints at one and the same moment, the return of Christ. It is “last” as the final summons of history, not the eighth of a series of secret raptures. The dictionary therefore marks it against the dispensational scheme that divides the coming of Christ into separate stages—a secret rapture before a tribulation and a later public appearing—for Scripture sets the resurrection of the dead, the changing of the living, and the gathering of the elect at one trumpet, the last. The doctrine is the comfort of the bereaved and the hope of the church: at the last trump the graves shall yield their dead, mortality shall put on immortality, and death shall be swallowed up in victory.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The final trumpet-blast at the coming of Christ, when the dead are raised incorruptible and the living changed in a moment (1 Corinthians 15:52; 1 Thessalonians 4:16); “last” as history's final summons, against a staged secret rapture.

LAST TRUMP, noun phrase. [Old French trompe, a trumpet.] The final trumpet-blast at the return of Christ.

“At the last trump… the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed” (1 Corinthians 15:52).

The Lord descends with the trump of God, and the dead in Christ rise first (1 Thessalonians 4:16).

Christ sends His angels with a great sound of a trumpet to gather the elect (Matthew 24:31).

“Last” as history's final summons, not one of a staged series of comings.

📖 Key Scripture

1 Co 15:52 — "In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed."

1 Th 4:16 — "For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:"

Mt 24:31 — "And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other."

1 Co 15:51 — "Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed,"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Dispensationalism divides the coming of Christ into a secret rapture and a later public appearing, against the single “last trump” that raises the dead and changes the living at one moment.

expand to see more

The dispensational scheme, a nineteenth-century novelty associated with Darby and Scofield, divides the second coming into two events separated by a seven-year tribulation: a secret rapture of the church, then a later public return. The dictionary rejects this on the plain testimony of the texts. Paul places the resurrection of the dead and the changing of the living at the last trump—a single, final, audible summons; the Lord descends with a shout and the trump of God, hardly a secret event; and the gathering of the elect is joined to the trumpet's great sound. To carve a hidden rapture out of these passages and postpone the public appearing is to read into Scripture a scheme it nowhere teaches.

The recovery is the unity and finality of the consummation. The last trump sounds once, and at its sounding the whole work is done: the dead in Christ rise, the living saints are transformed, the elect are gathered, and the Lord is openly revealed. The dictionary holds this against the speculative timetables and prophecy-charts that have led many astray, and rests the church's hope where the apostle rests it—not in escaping tribulation by a secret removal, but in the sure and public coming of Christ, when mortality shall put on immortality and death be swallowed up in victory. This hope the apostle commends as comfort: wherefore comfort one another with these words.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Greek salpinx (trumpet) and eschate salpinx (“the last trumpet”); the trumpet is the recurring biblical signal of God's presence, summons, and the consummation.

expand to see more

Salpinx, Greek, a trumpet, the instrument of God's summons.

Eschate salpinx, “the last trumpet,” the final blast of 1 Corinthians 15:52.

Shophar, the Hebrew ram's-horn trumpet of Sinai and the jubilee.

“In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye” (Greek en atomo) marks the change as instantaneous.

The “shout” (Greek keleusma) and “voice of the archangel” show the coming to be public, not secret.

Usage

"The pastor comforted the bereaved with the last trump, when the dead in Christ shall rise incorruptible."

"He showed that one trumpet raises the dead and changes the living, against the two-stage dispensational coming."

"She looked for the last trump, when mortality shall put on immortality and death be swallowed up in victory."
